chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majilawayh narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, who said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abi al-Jarud from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever says 'Subhanallah' (Glory be to Allah), Allah will plant for him a tree in Paradise by it; and whoever says 'Alhamdulillah' (Praise be to Allah), Allah will plant for him a tree in Paradise by it; and whoever says 'La ilaha illallah' (There is no god but Allah), Allah will plant for him a tree in Paradise by it; and whoever says 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah is the Greatest), Allah will plant for him a tree in Paradise by it.
A man from Quraish said: O Messenger of Allah, then our trees in Paradise would be many? He said: Yes, but beware that you do not send fire upon them so that it burns them.
And that is because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: O you who believe! Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not nullify your deeds.

key_terms.اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ: Allah is the Greatest (a form of dhikr)
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: Praise be to Allah (a form of dhikr)
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: Glory be to Allah (a form of dhikr)
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah (a form of dhikr)
key_terms.وَلَا تُبْطِلُوا أَعْمَالَكُمْ: And do not nullify your deeds (Quranic reference)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting the four Tasbihat and how can it be lost?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* highlights the spiritual fruitfulness of the four Tasbihat, using the metaphor of planting trees in Paradise to signify enduring rewards. The Prophet (peace be upon him) clarifies that while these recitations generate abundant merit, they remain vulnerable to nullification (*ibtal*) through disobedience, specifically linking the act to the Quranic warning against invalidating one's deeds. This underscores the Shia emphasis on the interplay between consistent dhikr and adherence to divine commandments.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: “One who says Sub- h’aanallah Allah will plant a tree for him in Paradise. One who says Al-h’amdulillaah  then too a tree will be planted for  him  in  Paradise.  Similarly,  One  who  says  Laa  ilaaha illallaah then also Allah will plant a tree for him in Paradise. Allah  will  also  plant  a tree for one who recites Allaahu Akbar.

A man of Quraish said: O the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.s.), then there would be many trees in Paradise for us? Yes,  but  be  careful  that  you  do  not  send  fire  or  they  all would get burnt up.
That is why the Almighty Allah said: O you who believe! Obey Allah and obey the Apostle, and do not make your deeds of no effect.1
